LS.L4.PSW.T01.title: Personal strengths
LS.L4.PSW.T01.description: Identifying own strengths, learning from successful and less successful experiences, using strengths to improve weaknesses.
LS.L4.PSW.T01.recovery_strategy: If the learner hesitates to name strengths, start with very concrete examples (running, drawing, helping others) and build up to abstract ones. Affirm that every learner has strengths and that strengths grow with practice.

questions.question: What is a 'strength'?
questions.ruby_prompt: Let's start simple. What does it mean when we say someone has a strength?
options: Something you are good at or do well
questions.expected: Something you are good at or do well
questions.memo: A strength is something you do well — like running fast, drawing, sharing, or learning a new song quickly.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of a strength?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at these and pick which one is a strength a person could have.
questions.expected: Being kind to others
questions.memo: Kindness is a strength — many strengths are about how we treat people, not just what we are clever at.

questions.question: True or false: Everybody has the same strengths.
questions.ruby_prompt: I want you to think about this one carefully. True or false: Everybody has the same strengths.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Each person has different strengths. One friend may be great at running while another is great at drawing — both are strengths.

questions.question: Thandi runs faster than anyone in her class. What is her strength?
questions.ruby_prompt: Thandi runs faster than anyone in her class. What is her strength?
questions.expected: Running
questions.memo: When you do something better than most people, that thing is one of your strengths. Running is Thandi's strength.

questions.question: Sipho always helps his friends when they fall. What is his strength?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho always helps his friends when they fall. What is his strength?
questions.expected: Kindness and caring
questions.memo: Helping others when they need it is a real strength — we call it kindness or caring.

questions.question: Name one thing you are good at.
questions.ruby_prompt: I'd love to hear about you. Tell me one thing that you are good at.
questions.expected: Running fast
questions.memo: Anything you do well counts — sport, drawing, kindness, helping at home, telling jokes, reading. Everyone has strengths.

questions.question: What should you do when you find something hard?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sometimes things are hard. What's a good thing to do when you find something hard?
options: Keep trying and ask for help
questions.expected: Keep trying and ask for help
questions.memo: Hard things become easier when we keep trying and ask for help. That is how a less successful experience becomes a learning experience.

questions.question: Your friend wins a singing competition. What should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Your friend wins a singing competition. What's the best thing for you to do?
options: Tell them well done — their strength makes you happy too
questions.expected: Tell them well done — their strength makes you happy too
questions.memo: Celebrating other people's strengths is part of being a good friend. Their win doesn't take anything away from your own strengths.

questions.question: Lerato wrote a maths test and got many wrong. What can she learn from this?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato wrote a maths test and got many wrong. What can she learn from this?
options: Which parts to practise more next time
That she should give up maths forever
questions.expected: Which parts to practise more next time
questions.memo: A less successful experience tells us what to practise. Getting things wrong is part of learning, not the end of it.

questions.question: Put these steps in the right order for turning a weakness into a strength.
questions.ruby_prompt: Drag these steps into the right order to turn a weakness into a strength.
questions.expected: Notice what is hard,Ask for help or practise,Keep practising over time,Notice it getting easier
questions.memo: First we notice what is hard. Then we practise or ask for help. Over time, with repeated practice, the thing becomes easier — and we have grown a new strength.

questions.question: Mpho won the school art competition. What is her strength?
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho won the school art competition. What is her strength?
questions.expected: Drawing and painting
questions.memo: Winning an art competition is a sign that Mpho's strength is drawing and painting.

questions.question: What does it mean to 'appreciate' a strength?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does it mean to 'appreciate' a strength?
options: To notice it and be glad about it
questions.expected: To notice it and be glad about it
questions.memo: Appreciate means to notice something good and feel glad. We can appreciate our own strengths and the strengths of others.

questions.question: Which is the best way to talk about your own strength?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is the best way to talk about something you are good at?
options: Say it kindly and also notice others' strengths
Say you are better than everyone else
Hide it and pretend you can't
Tell people they are bad at it
questions.expected: Say it kindly and also notice others' strengths
questions.memo: Owning your strength is good, but bragging hurts friendships. Notice your strength AND notice others'.

questions.question: Your friend is better at maths than you. How can you feel proud and happy?
questions.ruby_prompt: Your friend is better at maths than you. How can you still feel proud of yourself?
options: Remember your own strengths in other things
questions.expected: Remember your own strengths in other things
questions.memo: Friends have different strengths. You don't have to be best at everything to feel proud — you have your own strengths too.

questions.question: Which is a better thing to say to yourself when reading is hard?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's a better thing to say to yourself when reading feels hard?
options: I am learning to read better every day
I am bad at reading and I'll never learn
questions.expected: I am learning to read better every day
questions.memo: How you talk to yourself shapes how you grow. 'I'm learning' helps your brain keep trying.

questions.question: Tell me about a time something went wrong, and what you learned.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me about a time when something didn't go well for you. What did you learn?
questions.expected: I forgot my homework and learned to pack my bag the night before
questions.memo: Less successful experiences are full of lessons. The lesson is the part you take with you next time.

questions.question: What makes a strength grow stronger?
questions.ruby_prompt: What helps a strength grow stronger over time?
questions.expected: Practice and trying again
questions.memo: Strengths grow with practice. The more you do something the better you get — even if it was hard at first.

questions.question: True or false: Practice helps strengths grow.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Practice helps strengths grow.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — practice is the way strengths grow. Even people born with talent practise hard.

questions.question: Lwazi loves telling stories and acting them out. Which club is best for him?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lwazi loves telling stories and acting them out. Which club would be best for him?
questions.expected: Drama club
questions.memo: Strengths point us to activities. Storytelling and acting are drama skills — drama club is a great match.

questions.question: When someone says 'well done' for something you worked hard at, what's a good response?
questions.ruby_prompt: When someone says 'well done' for something you worked hard at, what's a kind thing to say back?
options: Thank you, I worked hard on it
I'm the best, nobody else could do it
questions.expected: Thank you, I worked hard on it
questions.memo: Accept the compliment with thanks. You don't have to brag, and you don't have to put yourself down.

LS.L4.PSW.T02.title: Respect for own and others' bodies
LS.L4.PSW.T02.description: Privacy and bodily integrity, caring for own body, respecting others' bodies, not subjecting one's body to substance abuse.
LS.L4.PSW.T02.recovery_strategy: Stay calm and matter-of-fact. Reinforce: your body belongs to you, you can say no to unwanted touch, and telling a trusted grown-up is always the right thing.

questions.question: Whose body is your body?
questions.ruby_prompt: Whose body is your body?
questions.expected: Mine — it belongs to me
questions.memo: Your body belongs to YOU. You get to decide who touches it and how.

questions.question: What does 'privacy' mean for your body?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does 'privacy' mean when we talk about your body?
options: The right to be alone when changing or in the bathroom
Hiding under a blanket all day
questions.expected: The right to be alone when changing or in the bathroom
questions.memo: Privacy means having your own space when you change clothes, use the toilet or shower. It is a normal and important right.

questions.question: Which is a good way to care for your body?
questions.ruby_prompt: Pick the good way to care for your body.
options: Wash, eat healthy food and get enough sleep
Stay up all night every night
questions.expected: Wash, eat healthy food and get enough sleep
questions.memo: Caring for your body means washing, eating good food, sleeping enough and being active. These are daily habits.

questions.question: Someone you don't know wants to hug you. What can you say?
questions.ruby_prompt: Someone you don't know wants to hug you. What is okay to say?
options: No thank you — and tell a trusted adult
questions.expected: No thank you — and tell a trusted adult
questions.memo: It's okay to say no to a hug, even from a grown-up. Tell a trusted adult so they know.

questions.question: Why should you respect other people's bodies?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it important to respect other people's bodies?
options: Because their body belongs to them, just like yours belongs to you
questions.expected: Because their body belongs to them, just like yours belongs to you
questions.memo: Respecting others' bodies is the same rule as respecting your own. Each person decides about their own body.

questions.question: Your friend says they don't want to be tickled. What should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Your friend says they don't want to be tickled. What should you do?
options: Stop and respect what they said
questions.expected: Stop and respect what they said
questions.memo: When someone says stop, we stop — even if we were having fun. That is respecting their body.

questions.question: Which of these can hurt your body if used wrongly?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these things can hurt your body if you use it the wrong way?
questions.expected: Tobacco, alcohol and other drugs
questions.memo: Tobacco, alcohol and drugs harm your body. Not putting them into your body is one way of respecting your body.

questions.question: What is a 'trusted adult'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does 'a trusted adult' mean?
options: A grown-up who looks after you and listens — like a parent, teacher or caregiver
questions.expected: A grown-up who looks after you and listens — like a parent, teacher or caregiver
questions.memo: A trusted adult is a grown-up who cares about you — a parent, guardian, teacher, religious leader, or school counsellor.

questions.question: If something feels wrong about how someone is touching you, what do you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: If something about how someone is touching you doesn't feel right, what do you do?
options: Say no, get away, and tell a trusted adult straight away
Promise to keep it a secret
questions.expected: Say no, get away, and tell a trusted adult straight away
questions.memo: If a touch feels wrong, your body is telling you something important. Say no, get away if you can, and tell a grown-up you trust.

questions.question: True or false: Secrets that make you feel scared or uncomfortable should be told to a trusted adult.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Secrets that make you feel scared or uncomfortable should be told to a trusted adult.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Happy surprise secrets (like a birthday present) are okay. Secrets that make you scared or uncomfortable are not okay to keep — tell a grown-up.

questions.question: Why should you not share a toothbrush with someone else?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is sharing a toothbrush not a good idea?
options: It can spread germs and diseases
questions.expected: It can spread germs and diseases
questions.memo: Toothbrushes touch our mouth, so they carry germs. Each person needs their own.

questions.question: Which of these is a way to respect your own body?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way to respect your own body?
options: Eat fresh food and get exercise
questions.expected: Eat fresh food and get exercise
questions.memo: Respecting your body means giving it good food and movement so it can grow well.

questions.question: An older person says, 'Don't tell anyone we hugged.' What should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Imagine an older person says, 'Don't tell anyone we hugged.' What should you do?
options: Tell a parent or teacher you trust — secret touches are not okay
questions.expected: Tell a parent or teacher you trust — secret touches are not okay
questions.memo: A trusted adult will help you. Touches that need to be kept secret are not safe — telling is the right thing.

questions.question: Why is sleep important for your body?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why does your body need sleep?
options: It helps your body grow and rest
It makes you taller right away
questions.expected: It helps your body grow and rest
questions.memo: While you sleep, your body grows, your brain saves what you learned, and your muscles rest. Children need about 9–11 hours.

questions.question: Put these steps in order for washing hands well.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these steps in order for washing hands properly.
questions.expected: Wet your hands,Use soap,Rub for 20 seconds,Rinse and dry
questions.memo: Wet first, then soap, then scrub all over for 20 seconds, then rinse and dry. This kills germs.

questions.question: A friend wants you to try a cigarette. What should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: A friend offers you a cigarette. What should you do?
options: Say no thank you and walk away — and tell a trusted adult
Ask if you can buy some
questions.expected: Say no thank you and walk away — and tell a trusted adult
questions.memo: Cigarettes harm your body badly. Saying no is respecting yourself. Telling an adult helps your friend too.

questions.question: When you are getting dressed, where is the best place?
questions.ruby_prompt: When you are changing your clothes, where is the best place?
options: In a private space like a bedroom or bathroom
In the middle of the playground
questions.expected: In a private space like a bedroom or bathroom
questions.memo: Privacy when changing protects your body and respects yourself. Public places aren't right for changing.

questions.question: Why must you protect your body from second-hand smoke?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it important to stay away from second-hand smoke?
options: Breathing other people's smoke also harms your lungs
Smoke is healthy if you don't see it
questions.expected: Breathing other people's smoke also harms your lungs
questions.memo: Even if you don't smoke yourself, breathing other people's smoke harms your lungs. Move to fresh air when you can.

questions.question: Tell me one rule you have for who can touch you.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one rule you have for who can touch you and how.
questions.expected: Only people I know and trust, and only in safe ways like a high-five or a family hug
questions.memo: Good answers might include: only family or close friends I trust; only safe touches like a hug from a parent; never any private parts. Your body, your rules.

questions.question: Karabo's cousin tells her to keep a touching incident a secret. What should Karabo do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo's cousin tells her to keep a touching incident a secret. What should Karabo do?
options: Tell a parent or teacher straight away
Wait a year before saying anything
questions.expected: Tell a parent or teacher straight away
questions.memo: Even when the person is family, secret touches that feel wrong must be told. A trusted adult will help — Karabo is not in trouble.

LS.L4.PSW.T03.title: Dealing with conflict
LS.L4.PSW.T03.description: Examples of conflict at home and school, strategies to avoid conflict, useful responses to conflict situations.
LS.L4.PSW.T03.recovery_strategy: Affirm that conflict is normal and can be handled. Walk through the steps — calm down, listen, talk, find a solution, ask an adult if needed. Avoid framing any feeling as wrong.

questions.question: What is a 'conflict'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does the word 'conflict' mean?
options: A disagreement or fight between people
questions.expected: A disagreement or fight between people
questions.memo: A conflict is when people disagree or fight. It can be small (sharing a pencil) or big (a serious argument).

questions.question: Which is an example of a conflict at home?
questions.ruby_prompt: Pick the example of a conflict that might happen at home.
options: You and your sister both want the last piece of bread
questions.expected: You and your sister both want the last piece of bread
questions.memo: Conflicts at home often start with sharing — food, the TV, chores. Other things in the list are not disagreements.

questions.question: Two friends both want to be team captain. This is an example of:
questions.ruby_prompt: Two friends both want to be team captain. What is this an example of?
questions.expected: A conflict at school
questions.memo: When two people want the same thing, that's a conflict. School has many — captain, partners, equipment.

questions.question: What is the FIRST thing to do when you feel angry in a conflict?
questions.ruby_prompt: When you feel angry in a fight, what is the first thing to do?
options: Stop and take a few deep breaths to calm down
questions.expected: Stop and take a few deep breaths to calm down
questions.memo: Calming down first stops the conflict from getting worse. Once you are calm you can think clearly.

questions.question: True or false: Hitting is a good way to win a conflict.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Hitting is a good way to win an argument.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Hitting makes things worse and is never the right answer. Words and calm thinking solve conflicts.

questions.question: Your brother takes your toy without asking. A useful response is to:
questions.ruby_prompt: Your brother takes your toy without asking. What's a useful thing to do?
options: Tell him calmly: 'Please give it back, I was using it'
Scream at the top of your voice
questions.expected: Tell him calmly: 'Please give it back, I was using it'
questions.memo: Speaking calmly and saying what you want is the best first step. Most conflicts can be solved with words.

questions.question: Put these steps in order for solving a conflict.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these steps in the right order to solve a conflict.
questions.expected: Calm down,Listen to the other person,Say how you feel,Find a fair solution together
questions.memo: Calm first, then listen, then share your side, then agree on what to do. Solutions stick when both sides feel heard.

questions.question: Which is a way to AVOID a conflict before it starts?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way to avoid a conflict before it starts?
options: Share, take turns and use kind words
Push to the front of the line
questions.expected: Share, take turns and use kind words
questions.memo: Sharing, taking turns and being kind keeps small disagreements from turning into big conflicts.

questions.question: You and your friend disagree about which game to play. A fair solution is to:
questions.ruby_prompt: You and your friend can't agree on which game to play. What's a fair solution?
options: Play your friend's choice first, then yours next
Play only your game and ignore them
questions.expected: Play your friend's choice first, then yours next
questions.memo: Taking turns is fair. Both people get what they want, just not at the same time.

questions.question: When a conflict feels too big to solve alone, what should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: When a fight feels too big for you to handle alone, what should you do?
options: Ask a trusted adult to help
questions.expected: Ask a trusted adult to help
questions.memo: Some conflicts need a grown-up to help — a parent, teacher or counsellor. Asking for help is smart, not weak.

questions.question: Which is an 'I-statement' that helps in a conflict?
questions.ruby_prompt: An 'I-statement' helps in a fight. Which of these is one?
options: 'I feel sad when you take my pencil without asking.'
questions.expected: 'I feel sad when you take my pencil without asking.'
questions.memo: 'I feel ... when ... because ...' tells the other person how you feel without blaming. Blame statements make conflicts bigger.

questions.question: Two classmates are arguing loudly. What's a good thing to do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Two classmates are arguing loudly. What's a good thing for you to do?
options: Tell a teacher so they can help sort it out safely
questions.expected: Tell a teacher so they can help sort it out safely
questions.memo: A teacher can help calm both sides. Joining in or laughing makes things worse.

questions.question: True or false: It's okay to walk away from a conflict to calm down.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: It's okay to walk away from a fight to calm down.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Walking away to cool off is wise. Come back to talk once both of you are calmer.

questions.question: Which response would make a conflict WORSE?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these would make a fight worse?
options: Calling the other person mean names
questions.expected: Calling the other person mean names
questions.memo: Name-calling adds hurt and grows the conflict. Listening, calm words, and walking away to cool off all help.

questions.question: After a conflict is solved, what's a good thing to do?
questions.ruby_prompt: After a fight is over, what's a good last step?
options: Say sorry for anything mean you said, and move on
Bring it up again every day
questions.expected: Say sorry for anything mean you said, and move on
questions.memo: A small 'sorry' for the hurt part helps friendships heal. Then both of you can move on.

questions.question: Lerato wants to use the swing. Sipho is already on it. A fair response is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato wants to use the swing. Sipho is already swinging on it. What is fair?
options: Lerato waits her turn or asks Sipho when he will be done
Lerato cries until she gets it
Lerato tells everyone Sipho is mean
questions.expected: Lerato waits her turn or asks Sipho when he will be done
questions.memo: Whoever was there first gets to finish their turn. Asking nicely or waiting is the fair way.

questions.question: Why does shouting usually NOT help in a conflict?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why does shouting usually not help in a fight?
options: It makes the other person feel attacked and they stop listening
questions.expected: It makes the other person feel attacked and they stop listening
questions.memo: Loud voices make others defensive — they stop listening and start defending. A calm voice gets you heard.

questions.question: Tell me a way you can stay calm when you're upset.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one way you stay calm when you feel upset.
questions.expected: Take deep breaths and count to ten
questions.memo: Good answers might include: deep breaths, counting, walking outside, drinking water, talking to a trusted adult.

questions.question: Your friend says something that hurts your feelings. The best first response is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Your friend says something that hurts your feelings. What's the best first response?
options: Tell them how it made you feel, using an I-statement
Pretend it didn't happen and stay angry
questions.expected: Tell them how it made you feel, using an I-statement
questions.memo: Sharing your feelings honestly is the best chance for them to understand and apologise.

questions.question: A conflict cannot always be 'won' — sometimes the best result is:
questions.ruby_prompt: A fight can't always be 'won.' Sometimes the best result is:
options: A solution where both people give a little
questions.expected: A solution where both people give a little
questions.memo: Compromise is when both sides give a bit so both get something. That keeps the friendship alive.

LS.L4.PSW.T04.title: Emotions: understanding a range of emotions
LS.L4.PSW.T04.description: Love, happiness, grief, fear and jealousy. Understanding own emotions and appropriate ways to express them, considering others' emotions.
LS.L4.PSW.T04.recovery_strategy: Normalise feelings — no emotion is wrong. Focus on naming the feeling and finding a healthy way to show it. If a learner is upset by content, slow down and check in.

questions.question: Which of these is an emotion?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is an emotion?
questions.expected: Happiness
questions.memo: Emotions are feelings inside us — happy, sad, angry, scared, jealous, in love.

questions.question: Which face shows happiness?
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the pictures. Which one shows a happy face?
questions.context: Pictures: a smiling face, a frowning face, a crying face, an angry face
questions.expected: Smiling face
questions.memo: A smile usually shows happiness. Faces show us a lot about how someone is feeling.

questions.question: When your grandmother passes away, the feeling you have is called:
questions.ruby_prompt: When someone we love passes away, the feeling we have is called what?
questions.expected: Grief
questions.memo: Grief is the deep sadness we feel when we lose someone we love. It is a real and important feeling.

questions.question: What is fear?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is fear?
options: The feeling of being scared of something
The feeling of being very full
questions.expected: The feeling of being scared of something
questions.memo: Fear is feeling scared — of the dark, of being alone, of getting hurt. It tells us to be careful.

questions.question: What is jealousy?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is jealousy?
questions.expected: Wanting something someone else has
questions.memo: Jealousy is when we want what someone else has — their toy, their score, their attention. Almost everyone feels it sometimes.

questions.question: True or false: It is okay to feel sad.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: It is okay to feel sad sometimes.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: All feelings are okay. Sad feelings come and go. What matters is how we show them.

questions.question: Sipho feels angry. Which is a healthy way to show it?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho feels angry. What's a healthy way for him to show that?
options: Take deep breaths and tell someone how he feels
questions.expected: Take deep breaths and tell someone how he feels
questions.memo: Anger is normal. Healthy ways to show it: breathe, name the feeling, talk to someone, move your body (run, dance).

questions.question: Your friend looks sad. What's a caring thing to do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Your friend looks really sad. What's a caring thing for you to do?
options: Ask if they're okay and listen
questions.expected: Ask if they're okay and listen
questions.memo: Caring for others' emotions starts with noticing and listening. You don't need to fix it — just being there helps.

questions.question: Which is a sign of love?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a sign of love between people?
options: Caring about how the other person feels
questions.expected: Caring about how the other person feels
questions.memo: Love shows in kindness, listening, caring about how the other person feels.

questions.question: Lerato is scared of the dark. The best thing she can do is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato is scared of the dark. What's the best thing she can do?
options: Tell a parent or use a small light to feel safer
questions.expected: Tell a parent or use a small light to feel safer
questions.memo: Fear is normal. Telling a grown-up and using a small comfort (a light, a soft toy) helps you feel safe.

questions.question: Match the situation to the feeling: 'My best friend moves to another town.'
questions.ruby_prompt: My best friend moves to another town. Which feeling fits best?
questions.expected: Sadness
questions.memo: Losing time with someone you love brings sadness. It is normal to feel this way.

questions.question: Tell me a healthy way to show that you are angry.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one healthy way to show that you are angry.
questions.expected: Take deep breaths and tell someone calmly
questions.memo: Good answers: deep breaths, count to ten, talk to someone, run or kick a ball, draw it out. Healthy = doesn't hurt yourself or anyone else.

questions.question: Why is it important to notice OTHER people's emotions?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it important to notice how other people are feeling?
options: So we can be kind and helpful to them
So we can laugh at them
questions.expected: So we can be kind and helpful to them
questions.memo: When we notice others' feelings, we can choose helpful actions — a smile, a kind word, a hug. That builds good friendships.

questions.question: Mpho is jealous because her sister got a new bike. A helpful response is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho is jealous because her sister got a new bike. What's a helpful thing for her to do?
options: Tell a parent how she's feeling and remember her own good things
questions.expected: Tell a parent how she's feeling and remember her own good things
questions.memo: Jealousy passes faster when we talk about it and remember good things in our own lives. Breaking or hitting won't help.

questions.question: Which of these can change a sad mood for the better?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these can help when you feel sad?
options: Talking to a friend or family member
questions.expected: Talking to a friend or family member
questions.memo: Sharing a sad feeling with a trusted person almost always helps. You don't have to hide it.

questions.question: True or false: Boys should never cry.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Boys should never cry.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: All people cry — boys, girls, men, women. Tears are a healthy way the body releases big feelings.

questions.question: Karabo's mom got a job in another city. Karabo feels:
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo's mom got a new job far away. The whole family is moving. Karabo might feel:
options: A mix of sad, excited and a little scared
Happy that she has to leave her friends
questions.expected: A mix of sad, excited and a little scared
questions.memo: Big changes often bring a mix of feelings at the same time — sad to leave friends, excited about something new, scared of the unknown. All of them are okay.

questions.question: Why do we have emotions?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do we have emotions?
options: They give us important information about us and the world
questions.expected: They give us important information about us and the world
questions.memo: Emotions are messengers. Fear says 'be careful', sadness says 'I need comfort', anger says 'something feels unfair'. They help us decide what to do.

questions.question: Which emotion might make you smile and laugh?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which emotion makes you smile and laugh?
questions.expected: Happiness
questions.memo: Happiness shows in smiles, laughter, and a feeling of warmth.

questions.question: A friend says something that makes you cry. They didn't mean to. What's a good response?
questions.ruby_prompt: A friend says something that hurts you, but they didn't mean it that way. What's a good response?
options: Tell them kindly that it hurt and explain why
questions.expected: Tell them kindly that it hurt and explain why
questions.memo: Speaking up kindly lets your friend learn. Most friends will say sorry and be more careful next time.

LS.L4.PSW.T05.title: Working in a group
LS.L4.PSW.T05.description: Working in a class, family or group project. Benefits and challenges of group work, useful responses to challenges.
LS.L4.PSW.T05.recovery_strategy: Lean on familiar groups — family, class group, school team. Remind the learner that groups work best when everyone contributes and disagreements are handled with respect.

questions.question: Which of these is a 'group'?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a group?
questions.expected: A family at home together
questions.memo: A group is two or more people doing something together. A family, a class, a sports team — all groups.

questions.question: What is a benefit of working in a group?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's a good thing about working in a group?
options: You can share ideas and finish faster
You always get the best mark
You don't have to do anything
questions.expected: You can share ideas and finish faster
questions.memo: Groups share ideas, share the work, and often produce better results than one person alone.

questions.question: Which is a challenge of working in a group?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's a challenge of working in a group?
options: People may disagree about what to do
There is no work to do
Everyone has the same exact ideas
questions.expected: People may disagree about what to do
questions.memo: Different people have different ideas, which is great but also tricky. Disagreement is the most common challenge.

questions.question: In a class project, one person is doing all the work. What should the group do?
questions.ruby_prompt: In a class project, one person is doing all the work. What should the group do?
options: Share out the tasks so everyone helps
Let one person carry on alone
questions.expected: Share out the tasks so everyone helps
questions.memo: Fair group work means everyone contributes. Sharing tasks is the answer when one person is overloaded.

questions.question: True or false: It's okay to disagree in a group as long as you stay respectful.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: It's okay to disagree in a group, as long as you stay respectful.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — disagreement is part of group work. The key is to stay respectful and listen to each other.

questions.question: What is a 'role' in a group project?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is a 'role' in a group project?
options: A specific job each person does
questions.expected: A specific job each person does
questions.memo: A role is your job in the group — researcher, writer, presenter. Roles help share the work fairly.

questions.question: Your group can't agree on a topic. The best way to decide is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Your group can't agree on a topic. What's the best way to decide?
options: Talk through everyone's ideas and vote
Don't decide and miss the deadline
questions.expected: Talk through everyone's ideas and vote
questions.memo: Listen to everyone, then vote. Fair voting is how groups make decisions when they disagree.

questions.question: Put these steps in order for a group project.
questions.ruby_prompt: Drag these into the right order for doing a group project.
questions.expected: Decide the topic together,Share out the tasks,Each person does their part,Bring the parts together
questions.memo: Decide together, split the work, each does their piece, then put it all together. That's how groups finish on time.

questions.question: Which is a sign of good listening in a group?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does good listening in a group look like?
options: Looking at the speaker and not interrupting
questions.expected: Looking at the speaker and not interrupting
questions.memo: Eye contact, no interrupting, nodding to show you hear them — that is good listening. People feel respected when listened to.

questions.question: Lerato is part of a project group at school. What is one thing she should do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato is in a group project at school. What's one thing she should do?
options: Do her part of the work on time
Hand it in late on purpose
Refuse to talk to her group
questions.expected: Do her part of the work on time
questions.memo: Doing your part on time keeps the group going. When one person drops out, the rest have to do more.

questions.question: Why does a family work better when everyone helps with chores?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why does a family work better when everyone helps with chores?
options: The work is shared so no one is too tired
questions.expected: The work is shared so no one is too tired
questions.memo: A family is also a group. Sharing chores means no one carries it all — fairer and kinder for everyone.

questions.question: Which response is helpful when a group-mate makes a mistake?
questions.ruby_prompt: When someone in your group makes a mistake, what's a helpful response?
options: Tell the teacher to fail them
questions.expected: Help them fix it kindly
questions.memo: Everyone makes mistakes. Helping kindly keeps the group strong; laughing or shaming breaks it down.

questions.question: Your sibling refuses to help wash dishes. What's a useful response?
questions.ruby_prompt: Your sibling refuses to help wash dishes. What's a useful thing to do?
options: Talk to a parent and explain fairly
Refuse to ever speak to them
questions.expected: Talk to a parent and explain fairly
questions.memo: When a family member won't pitch in, a parent can help sort it out fairly. Talking is better than fighting.

questions.question: What does 'compromise' mean in a group?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does it mean to 'compromise' in a group?
options: Each person gives a little so the group can agree
questions.expected: Each person gives a little so the group can agree
questions.memo: Compromise = meet in the middle. Both sides give a bit, and the group moves forward.

questions.question: True or false: A quiet group member has nothing useful to say.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: A quiet group member has nothing useful to say.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Quiet people often have great ideas — they just need a chance. Asking them what they think helps the group.

questions.question: Tell me one job you can do to help your family.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one job you can do to help your family at home.
questions.expected: Washing dishes or sweeping the floor
questions.memo: Examples: washing dishes, sweeping, making the bed, looking after a younger brother or sister, helping cook. Every bit helps.

questions.question: Mpho's group is loud and getting nothing done. What can she do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho's group is loud and getting nothing done. What can she do?
options: Calmly ask the group to focus on the task
questions.expected: Calmly ask the group to focus on the task
questions.memo: Even one person staying calm can pull a noisy group back to work. Sometimes a quiet, focused voice is the loudest.

questions.question: Why is it important to say 'thank you' in a group?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it important to say 'thank you' in a group?
options: It tells people their work is noticed and valued
questions.expected: It tells people their work is noticed and valued
questions.memo: A 'thank you' makes people feel seen. Groups where people feel valued work better.

questions.question: Which group has the BEST chance of finishing a project well?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which group has the best chance of finishing a project well?
options: One where everyone listens, shares tasks and helps each other
One where one person bosses everyone
questions.expected: One where everyone listens, shares tasks and helps each other
questions.memo: Listening + sharing + helping = strong group. Bossing or silence or fighting = weak group.

questions.question: Your group finishes their project. What's a good last step together?
questions.ruby_prompt: Your group has just finished a project. What's a good last step to do together?
options: Thank each other for the work and notice what went well
Argue about who did the most
Blame one person for any mistakes
questions.expected: Thank each other for the work and notice what went well
questions.memo: Celebrating the work together makes the group want to work together again. Blaming makes future groups harder.

LS.L4.PSW.T06.title: Bullying: appropriate responses
LS.L4.PSW.T06.description: Recognising acts of bullying, appropriate responses, where to find help.
LS.L4.PSW.T06.recovery_strategy: Bullying content can stir up real feelings. Stay calm, validate that being bullied is never the learner's fault, and always reinforce that telling a trusted adult is the right thing — never tattling.

questions.question: What is bullying?
questions.ruby_prompt: Let's start with the word. What is bullying?
options: Hurting someone on purpose, again and again
Telling a teacher about a problem
questions.expected: Hurting someone on purpose, again and again
questions.memo: Bullying is on-purpose hurt that happens more than once — hitting, name-calling, leaving someone out, spreading rumours.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of bullying?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is bullying?
options: Calling someone names every day at school
questions.expected: Calling someone names every day at school
questions.memo: Daily name-calling is bullying — it hurts on purpose and keeps happening. The other options are kindness, not bullying.

questions.question: True or false: Leaving someone out of games on purpose is bullying.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Leaving someone out of games on purpose, every day, is a kind of bullying.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Bullying isn't only hitting and shouting. Leaving someone out, on purpose and again and again, also hurts and counts as bullying.

questions.question: Someone is bullying you. What is the BEST thing to do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Someone is bullying you. What is the best thing to do?
options: Tell a trusted adult — a parent, teacher or counsellor
Pretend it doesn't bother you for years
Hide and never come back to school
questions.expected: Tell a trusted adult — a parent, teacher or counsellor
questions.memo: Telling a trusted adult is the strongest move. They can help you and stop the bullying. You are not in trouble — you are getting help.

questions.question: Telling an adult about bullying is the same as 'tattling.' True or false?
questions.ruby_prompt: Telling an adult about bullying is the same as tattling. True or false?
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Tattling is to get someone in trouble for something small. Telling about bullying is to keep someone safe. They are not the same.

questions.question: Who is a 'trusted adult' you can tell about bullying?
questions.ruby_prompt: Who is a trusted adult you could tell about bullying?
options: A parent, teacher, school counsellor or religious leader
questions.expected: A parent, teacher, school counsellor or religious leader
questions.memo: Trusted adults are grown-ups in your life who care about you and listen — a parent, teacher, counsellor, family member, or religious leader.

questions.question: Sipho sees Lerato being pushed and called names every day. What's the right thing for him to do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho sees Lerato being pushed and called names every day. What's the right thing for him to do?
options: Tell a teacher and be kind to Lerato
Walk past and ignore it forever
questions.expected: Tell a teacher and be kind to Lerato
questions.memo: Bystanders matter. Telling an adult and showing kindness to the person being bullied is powerful — bullies stop when others speak up.

questions.question: Bullying that happens on phones or online is called:
questions.ruby_prompt: Bullying that happens on phones or online has a special name. What is it?
questions.expected: Cyberbullying
questions.memo: Cyberbullying is bullying through messages, comments or social media. It is just as serious as in-person bullying.

questions.question: If you get mean messages on a phone, what should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: If you start getting mean messages on a phone, what should you do?
options: Save the messages and tell a trusted adult
Send them to all your friends
Delete everything and tell no one
questions.expected: Save the messages and tell a trusted adult
questions.memo: Saving the messages is proof, and the adult can help stop it. Don't reply — that often makes the bully more excited.

questions.question: Is bullying ever the fault of the person being bullied?
questions.ruby_prompt: Is bullying ever the fault of the person being bullied?
options: No — it is never the fault of the person being bullied
questions.expected: No — it is never the fault of the person being bullied
questions.memo: Bullying is always the bully's choice. The person being bullied is never to blame for who they are or how they look.

questions.question: Which of these helps STOP bullying at a school?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these helps stop bullying at a school?
options: Students and teachers speak up when they see it
questions.expected: Students and teachers speak up when they see it
questions.memo: Bullying stops when the silent majority speaks up. One person speaking out helps; many speaking out works wonders.

questions.question: True or false: It is okay to fight back with fists when bullied.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: It is okay to fight back with fists when someone bullies you.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Fighting back can hurt both of you and may get you into trouble too. Stronger answer: get away, tell a trusted adult.

questions.question: Bullying can hurt in many ways. Which is NOT a way bullying hurts?
questions.ruby_prompt: Bullying hurts in many ways. Which of these is NOT a way bullying hurts?
options: By making you better at maths
By making you scared to go to school
By making you feel sad and alone
questions.expected: By making you better at maths
questions.memo: Bullying never improves anyone — it hurts the heart, the mind, sometimes the body. None of that is good for you.

questions.question: Where can South African children call for help with bullying or abuse?
questions.ruby_prompt: Where in South Africa can a child call for help with bullying or abuse?
questions.expected: Childline South Africa: 116
questions.memo: Childline 116 is a free national helpline in South Africa, just for children, that you can call any time. They listen and help.

questions.question: Karabo's friend is being bullied but says, 'Don't tell anyone.' What should Karabo do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo's friend is being bullied but says, 'Please don't tell anyone.' What should Karabo do?
options: Tell a trusted adult anyway — keeping bullying secret allows it to continue
questions.expected: Tell a trusted adult anyway — keeping bullying secret allows it to continue
questions.memo: Some secrets are dangerous. Bullying is one. Telling a trusted adult is being a real friend, even if your friend asks you not to.

questions.question: Mpho feels like nobody likes her because the bullying has gone on for a long time. What's important for her to know?
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho feels like nobody likes her because the bullying has gone on for a long time. What's important for her to know?
options: She is not alone, help is real, and the bullying is not her fault
She must change everything about herself
questions.expected: She is not alone, help is real, and the bullying is not her fault
questions.memo: Bullying lies — it makes the person feel alone and broken. The truth: it isn't her fault, there are people who care, and there is help.

questions.question: Tell me one thing you can do if you see someone being bullied.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one thing you can do if you see someone being bullied at school.
questions.expected: Tell a teacher and be kind to the person being bullied
questions.memo: Good answers: tell a teacher, sit with the person at lunch, walk them home, say 'leave them alone' if safe, save messages as proof.

questions.question: Bullies usually bully others because:
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do you think bullies usually bully other people?
options: They are often unhappy or hurting too, even if they don't show it
questions.expected: They are often unhappy or hurting too, even if they don't show it
questions.memo: Most bullies are not happy people. They often have their own pain. That does not excuse the bullying — but it helps us see bullies clearly.

questions.question: Put these steps in order for what to do if you are bullied.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for what to do if you are being bullied.
options: Talk to a counsellor if the feelings stay
questions.expected: Get to a safe place,Tell a trusted adult,Save any proof (messages, photos),Talk to a counsellor if the feelings stay
questions.memo: Safe first, then tell, then save proof, then look after how you feel inside. That gives you safety, action and healing.

questions.question: Which is the most important thing to remember if you are being bullied?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is the most important thing to remember if you are being bullied?
options: You are not alone and it is not your fault — help is real
You must keep it secret forever
questions.expected: You are not alone and it is not your fault — help is real
questions.memo: These three truths are bigger than the bullying: you are not alone, it is not your fault, and there is real help. Hold onto them.

LS.L4.PSW.T07.title: Children's rights and responsibilities
LS.L4.PSW.T07.description: Rights to name, health, safety, education, shelter, food and a safe environment as stipulated in the SA Constitution; matching responsibilities.
LS.L4.PSW.T07.recovery_strategy: Anchor in concrete examples from school and home. Every right has a matching responsibility — link them together when the learner is confused.

questions.question: What is a 'right'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does it mean when we say children have a 'right'?
options: Something every child should have, just because they are a child
Something you earn by being good
questions.expected: Something every child should have, just because they are a child
questions.memo: Rights belong to all children, no matter who they are. The SA Constitution lists them and protects them.

questions.question: Which of these is a children's right?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a right that all children have?
options: The right to stay up forever
questions.expected: The right to an education
questions.memo: Every child has the right to go to school. The SA Constitution and the Children's Act protect this right.

questions.question: Which is a child's right about their identity?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a right about who a child is?
options: The right to a name and to be known
The right to change name every week
The right to have no parents
questions.expected: The right to a name and to be known
questions.memo: Every child has the right to a name and a recorded identity. This is the start of being known and protected.

questions.question: Children have the right to:
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a child's right?
options: Be hit when they are noisy
questions.expected: Be safe from harm
questions.memo: Safety is a basic right. No one is allowed to hurt a child, by law and by the Constitution.

questions.question: What is a 'responsibility'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is a responsibility?
options: Something you should do, often to match a right
Something you don't have to do
questions.expected: Something you should do, often to match a right
questions.memo: Responsibilities are the actions that go with rights. The right to learn comes with the responsibility to try at school.

questions.question: Match the right and responsibility: 'I have the right to an education. My responsibility is...'
questions.ruby_prompt: Match the right with the right responsibility. 'I have the right to an education. My responsibility is...'
options: To go to school and try my best
To skip class whenever I want
questions.expected: To go to school and try my best
questions.memo: If you have the right to learn, you also take responsibility for showing up and trying. Rights and responsibilities work together.

questions.question: Children have the right to:
questions.ruby_prompt: Pick a right that children have.
questions.expected: Food and shelter
questions.memo: Food, shelter and basic care are rights for every child. Driving and voting come later in life.

questions.question: True or false: Children's rights are the same for all children in South Africa.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Children's rights are the same for ALL children in South Africa.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. The Constitution protects every child equally, no matter their race, gender, language or where they live.

questions.question: Lerato has the right to a clean and safe environment. Her responsibility is to:
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato has the right to a clean and safe environment. What's her matching responsibility?
options: Not litter and look after her surroundings
questions.expected: Not litter and look after her surroundings
questions.memo: A clean environment is everyone's responsibility too. Picking up litter and caring for nature matches the right.

questions.question: Which is part of the right to health?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's part of the right to health for children?
options: Going to a clinic when you are sick
questions.expected: Going to a clinic when you are sick
questions.memo: Health care, vaccines and clean water are all parts of the right to health. Free clinics are open to all children in SA.

questions.question: Which document in South Africa protects children's rights?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which big rulebook in South Africa protects children's rights?
questions.expected: The Constitution
questions.memo: The South African Constitution is the highest law of the country. It includes a special section on children's rights.

questions.question: If a child is not getting enough food at home, what should happen?
questions.ruby_prompt: If a child is not getting enough food at home, what should happen?
options: A trusted adult, social worker or Childline should be told so they can help
The child must just be hungry
questions.expected: A trusted adult, social worker or Childline should be told so they can help
questions.memo: Food is a child's right. If it isn't there, telling a trusted adult or Childline (116) brings help — the family can be supported.

questions.question: Sipho has the right to be heard. His responsibility is to:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho has the right to be heard. What is his matching responsibility?
options: Listen to others when they speak
questions.expected: Listen to others when they speak
questions.memo: Being heard is a right; listening is the matching responsibility. Conversation goes both ways.

questions.question: Children have the right to:
questions.ruby_prompt: Pick another children's right.
options: Work all day in dangerous jobs
questions.expected: Play and rest
questions.memo: Children have the right to play and rest. Heavy work for children is against the law in South Africa.

questions.question: Match the right to its example: 'The right to shelter.'
questions.ruby_prompt: Match this right to its example. The right to shelter means:
questions.expected: A safe place to live
questions.memo: Shelter means a safe place to live — a roof, walls, somewhere away from danger.

questions.question: Tell me one of YOUR responsibilities as a child.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one of your own responsibilities as a child.
questions.expected: Going to school and doing my homework
questions.memo: Good answers: going to school, doing homework, helping at home, being kind, looking after siblings, telling the truth.

questions.question: True or false: Children have rights AND responsibilities — both together.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Children have rights AND responsibilities — both together.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes — rights and responsibilities are two sides of the same coin. Free people are also responsible people.

questions.question: Karabo's right to safety is being broken at home — someone is hurting her. What should happen?
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo is being hurt at home. What is the right thing to do?
options: Tell a teacher, social worker or Childline (116) — Karabo will be helped
questions.expected: Tell a teacher, social worker or Childline (116) — Karabo will be helped
questions.memo: When a right is being broken, telling a trusted adult or Childline opens up help. Karabo deserves safety, and there are people whose job it is to help.

questions.question: Put these in the right order for what to do if your rights are being broken.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for what to do if your rights are being broken.
options: Notice the right is being broken
Get help from a social worker or Childline if needed
Stay safe while the adults take action
questions.expected: Notice the right is being broken,Tell a trusted adult,Get help from a social worker or Childline if needed,Stay safe while the adults take action
questions.memo: Notice, tell, get help, stay safe. Rights are real and there are real people whose job is to protect them — Childline 116 is one.

questions.question: Why do rights and responsibilities go together?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do you think rights and responsibilities go together?
options: My rights are protected when I respect others' rights too
questions.expected: My rights are protected when I respect others' rights too
questions.memo: Society works because everyone respects each other's rights. Your right to be safe rests on others not hurting you — and them having the same right.

LS.L4.PSW.T08.title: Cultures and moral lessons
LS.L4.PSW.T08.description: Cultural groups in SA, menus from different cultures, moral lessons drawn from the narratives of cultural groups.
LS.L4.PSW.T08.recovery_strategy: Treat every culture with equal respect. Use the learner's own culture as a starting point and explore others alongside it. Avoid ranking or stereotyping.

questions.question: What is a 'culture'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What do we mean by 'culture'?
options: A group's way of life — their language, food, music and beliefs
questions.expected: A group's way of life — their language, food, music and beliefs
questions.memo: Culture is the shared way of life of a group — how they speak, eat, dress, celebrate and what they believe.

questions.question: Which of these is a South African food?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a South African dish?
questions.expected: Pap and stew
questions.memo: Pap (made from mealies) with stew is a common South African meal across many cultures. The others are dishes from other countries.

questions.question: Bobotie is a dish from which culture in South Africa?
questions.ruby_prompt: Bobotie is a famous South African dish. Where does it come from?
questions.expected: Cape Malay culture
questions.memo: Bobotie — minced meat with a creamy egg topping and spices — is a Cape Malay dish, an important part of SA food heritage.

questions.question: Umngqusho (samp and beans) is part of which cultural food tradition?
questions.ruby_prompt: Umngqusho — samp and beans — is part of which South African food tradition?
questions.expected: Xhosa
questions.memo: Umngqusho is a traditional Xhosa dish of samp (broken dried maize) and sugar beans. It was a favourite of Nelson Mandela.

questions.question: Which of these is a 'moral lesson' in a folk story?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a moral lesson — a teaching — that a folk story might give?
options: Be kind to strangers, you don't know who they are
questions.expected: Be kind to strangers, you don't know who they are
questions.memo: Moral lessons are the teachings inside stories — about how to be a good person. Kindness, honesty and bravery are common ones.

questions.question: True or false: All cultures in South Africa are equal under the Constitution.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: All cultures in South Africa are equal under the Constitution.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. The Constitution protects all cultures equally. None is above another.

questions.question: Mpho's friend speaks isiZulu at home. Mpho's family speaks Sesotho. What's true?
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho's friend speaks isiZulu at home. Mpho's family speaks Sesotho. What's a true statement?
options: Both families are South African and have rich cultures
Only one of them is really South African
One culture is better than the other
questions.expected: Both families are South African and have rich cultures
questions.memo: South Africa has 11 official languages and many cultures. Different cultures don't make people less South African — they make our country rich.

questions.question: Many African folk stories include animals like:
questions.ruby_prompt: Many African folk stories feature certain animals. Which is one?
options: The hare or tortoise (who is clever)
questions.expected: The hare or tortoise (who is clever)
questions.memo: Hare and Tortoise stories appear across many African cultures. They usually teach a lesson about cleverness, patience, or honesty.

questions.question: What does respecting a culture you don't know much about look like?
questions.ruby_prompt: How do you show respect for a culture you don't know much about?
questions.expected: Ask polite questions and listen
questions.memo: Respect starts with curiosity. Polite questions and listening show that another culture matters to you.

questions.question: Biltong is a dried meat snack from which heritage?
questions.ruby_prompt: Biltong is a dried meat snack. It comes from which South African heritage?
questions.expected: Afrikaner / Voortrekker tradition
questions.memo: Biltong was developed by early Dutch settlers and Voortrekkers as a way to preserve meat. It's now eaten across all SA cultures.

questions.question: Tell me one food from your culture or family.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one food that your family or culture eats often.
questions.expected: Pap and chicken stew
questions.memo: Good answers: any food your family eats — pap, samp, curry, bobotie, biltong, vetkoek, rice and stew. Food carries family stories.

questions.question: A folk story tells of a greedy person who loses everything. The moral lesson is:
questions.ruby_prompt: In a folk story, a greedy person ends up losing everything they had. What's the moral lesson?
options: Don't be greedy — sharing keeps you well
questions.expected: Don't be greedy — sharing keeps you well
questions.memo: Many stories warn against greed. The lesson sticks because we see the outcome happen to the character.

questions.question: Why do many cultures tell similar moral stories?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do many different cultures tell similar moral stories?
options: Because people everywhere face similar challenges — kindness, honesty, courage
Because there are only three stories
questions.expected: Because people everywhere face similar challenges — kindness, honesty, courage
questions.memo: People everywhere ask the same big questions about being good — so similar lessons appear in cultures that have never met.

questions.question: Which is part of Zulu cultural heritage?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is part of Zulu cultural heritage?
questions.expected: Zulu reed dance
questions.memo: The Zulu reed dance (Umkhosi woMhlanga) is an annual cultural event in KwaZulu-Natal that celebrates young women.

questions.question: Cape Malay culture's roots in South Africa come from:
questions.ruby_prompt: Where do Cape Malay culture's roots in South Africa come from?
options: Enslaved and freed people brought from places like Indonesia, Malaysia and India
questions.expected: Enslaved and freed people brought from places like Indonesia, Malaysia and India
questions.memo: Cape Malay culture was shaped by the people brought to the Cape during slavery, mostly from southeast Asia. Their language, food and faith all enriched SA.

questions.question: Put these in order to retell a folk story to a friend.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order — how to retell a folk story to a friend.
questions.expected: Set the scene (who and where),What happens,How it ends,The moral lesson
questions.memo: Setting, action, ending, lesson — that's the shape of a good story-retell.

questions.question: A story ends with: 'The lion learned that even small friends can save you.' The moral lesson is:
questions.ruby_prompt: A story ends like this: 'The lion learned that even small friends can save you.' What is the moral lesson?
options: Don't look down on others because they are small
questions.expected: Don't look down on others because they are small
questions.memo: This is the lesson from the famous 'Lion and the Mouse' story. Size doesn't decide who is helpful — even a small mouse helped the lion.

questions.question: True or false: Learning about other cultures takes away your own culture.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Learning about other cultures takes away your own culture.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Learning about another culture doesn't erase yours — it adds to what you know. Many South Africans live in more than one cultural world.

questions.question: Which is a way to celebrate cultural diversity at school?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way to celebrate cultural diversity at school?
options: A heritage day where everyone shares food, music or stories
questions.expected: A heritage day where everyone shares food, music or stories
questions.memo: Heritage Day (24 September) is South Africa's national celebration of cultural diversity. Schools often hold their own version.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'I am because we are' (Ubuntu) mean?
questions.ruby_prompt: Ubuntu is an African saying: 'I am because we are.' What does it mean?
options: We are who we are because of the people around us
questions.expected: We are who we are because of the people around us
questions.memo: Ubuntu teaches that we belong together. My kindness shapes you; yours shapes me. It's a deep cultural value across southern Africa.

LS.L4.PSW.T09.title: Major religions in South Africa
LS.L4.PSW.T09.description: Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism, Baha'i Faith and African Religion. Significant places, buildings and worship symbols.
LS.L4.PSW.T09.recovery_strategy: Stay neutral and respectful — every religion gets equal respect. The goal is to RECOGNISE names, symbols and places, not to compare or rank.

questions.question: What is a 'religion'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is a religion?
options: A shared set of beliefs about God, life and how to live
questions.expected: A shared set of beliefs about God, life and how to live
questions.memo: Religions share beliefs about God or a higher power, sacred stories and ways to live. Many people in SA follow a religion.

questions.question: Which place do Christians go to worship?
questions.ruby_prompt: Where do Christians go to worship?
questions.expected: Church
questions.memo: Christians worship in a church. Different Christian groups have different styles of churches.

questions.question: Which place do Muslims go to worship?
questions.ruby_prompt: Where do Muslims go to worship?
questions.expected: Mosque
questions.memo: Muslims pray in a mosque. The biggest mosque in SA is the Houghton Mosque, but mosques are in cities and towns across the country.

questions.question: Which place do Jewish people go to worship?
questions.ruby_prompt: Where do Jewish people go to worship?
questions.expected: Synagogue
questions.memo: Jewish people worship in a synagogue. Most South African synagogues are in Cape Town and Johannesburg.

questions.question: Which place do Hindus go to worship?
questions.ruby_prompt: Where do Hindus go to worship?
questions.expected: Hindu temple (mandir)
questions.memo: Hindus worship in a temple, often called a 'mandir'. KwaZulu-Natal has many famous Hindu temples.

questions.question: The cross is a symbol of which religion?
questions.ruby_prompt: The cross is a symbol of which religion?
questions.expected: Christianity
questions.memo: The cross reminds Christians of Jesus and is the main symbol of their faith.

questions.question: The Star of David is a symbol of which religion?
questions.ruby_prompt: The Star of David is a symbol of which religion?
questions.expected: Judaism
questions.memo: The Star of David is a six-pointed star and the main symbol of Judaism.

questions.question: The crescent moon and star is a symbol often linked with which religion?
questions.ruby_prompt: The crescent moon and star is a symbol often linked with which religion?
questions.expected: Islam
questions.memo: The crescent moon and star is often used to represent Islam, though Islam itself does not have one fixed symbol.

questions.question: Which symbol is linked with Hinduism?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a symbol of Hinduism?
questions.expected: Om (ॐ)
questions.memo: 'Om' is a sacred sound and symbol in Hinduism — many Hindu prayers begin with it.

questions.question: Buddhism began with a teacher called:
questions.ruby_prompt: Buddhism began with the teachings of a person known as:
questions.expected: The Buddha
questions.memo: The Buddha was a teacher who lived in ancient India. Buddhism comes from his teachings about kindness, calm and seeing things clearly.

questions.question: African Religion is practised across South Africa. One feature of it is:
questions.ruby_prompt: African Religion is practised across South Africa. What is one feature of it?
options: Respect for ancestors as part of family life
questions.expected: Respect for ancestors as part of family life
questions.memo: African Religion in SA includes honouring ancestors — family members who have died but who are still cared for through rituals and memory.

questions.question: The Baha'i Faith teaches that:
questions.ruby_prompt: The Baha'i Faith teaches that...
options: All people are one human family
Only one group of people matters
questions.expected: All people are one human family
questions.memo: The Baha'i Faith teaches the unity of humankind — that all people are one family, no matter their religion, race or language.

questions.question: True or false: South Africa has many religions, all protected by the Constitution.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: South Africa has many religions, all protected by the Constitution.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. The Constitution protects freedom of religion — you may follow any faith, change faith, or follow none.

questions.question: When a classmate's religion is different from yours, the respectful thing is to:
questions.ruby_prompt: When a classmate's religion is different from yours, what is the respectful thing to do?
questions.expected: Listen and ask polite questions
questions.memo: Curiosity with kindness is the way. Different doesn't mean worse — your friend's religion is part of who they are.

questions.question: Match symbol to religion: a star and crescent moon.
questions.ruby_prompt: Pictures: a cross, a Star of David, a crescent moon and star, an Om symbol. Which religion is linked with the crescent moon and star?
questions.context: Pictures: a cross, a Star of David, a crescent moon and star, an Om symbol
questions.expected: Islam
questions.memo: The crescent moon and star is widely linked to Islam, especially on flags of Muslim-majority countries.

questions.question: Match symbol to religion: the cross.
questions.ruby_prompt: Look at the same pictures. Which religion is linked with the cross?
questions.context: Pictures: a cross, a Star of David, a crescent moon and star, an Om symbol
questions.expected: Christianity
questions.memo: The cross is the main symbol of Christianity. It reminds Christians of Jesus.

questions.question: Why do many people read or recite from sacred books in worship?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do many people read from sacred books when they worship?
options: Sacred books carry the teachings of their faith
There is nothing else to do
questions.expected: Sacred books carry the teachings of their faith
questions.memo: The Bible, Qur'an, Torah, Vedas and Tripitaka all hold the central teachings of their religion. Reading from them is part of worship.

questions.question: Tell me the name of a religion practised in South Africa.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me the name of a religion practised in South Africa.
questions.expected: Christianity
questions.memo: Good answers: Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Judaism, Buddhism, Baha'i Faith, African Religion. All of these are practised in SA.

questions.question: Which is a kind action that almost ALL religions teach?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which kind action is taught by almost all religions?
options: Treat others the way you want to be treated
questions.expected: Treat others the way you want to be treated
questions.memo: This 'golden rule' is found across nearly all religions and cultures. It's the heart of how to live with other people.

questions.question: A Hindu temple, a Christian church, a mosque and a synagogue are all examples of:
questions.ruby_prompt: A Hindu temple, a Christian church, a mosque and a synagogue are all examples of what?
questions.expected: Places of worship
questions.memo: Places of worship are buildings where people gather to pray together. Different religions have different names for them.

LS.L4.PSW.T10.title: Dangers in and around water
LS.L4.PSW.T10.description: Home and public swimming pools, rivers and dams; responsible safety measures in and around water.
LS.L4.PSW.T10.recovery_strategy: Reinforce: water can be dangerous even when it looks calm; never swim alone; always tell a grown-up where you are.

questions.question: Which water place can be dangerous?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these places can be dangerous if you are not careful?
options: A river, a dam and a swimming pool
A cooking pot of cold food
questions.expected: A river, a dam and a swimming pool
questions.memo: Any deep water can be dangerous if you don't take care — rivers, dams, pools and even buckets for very small children.

questions.question: True or false: You should always swim with a grown-up watching.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: You should always swim with a grown-up watching.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Even if you are a strong swimmer, a grown-up watching can save your life if something goes wrong.

questions.question: What is the safest thing to do if a friend falls into deep water and can't swim?
questions.ruby_prompt: Your friend falls into deep water and can't swim. What's the SAFEST thing to do?
options: Shout for help and throw something they can hold onto
questions.expected: Shout for help and throw something they can hold onto
questions.memo: Jumping in usually makes things worse — drowning people can pull rescuers down. Shout for help, throw a rope, stick or float.

questions.question: Which of these is a safe action around a swimming pool?
questions.ruby_prompt: Pick the safe action around a swimming pool.
options: Walk, don't run, near the pool edge
Run and jump where you can't see
questions.expected: Walk, don't run, near the pool edge
questions.memo: Wet tiles around a pool are slippery — walking, not running, prevents falls and head bumps.

questions.question: A river looks calm on top, but underneath it can have:
questions.ruby_prompt: A river looks calm on top, but underneath it can have what danger?
options: Strong currents that pull you under
questions.expected: Strong currents that pull you under
questions.memo: Rivers can have hidden currents — water that moves under the surface. They can pull even strong adults under.

questions.question: What should you do BEFORE swimming in any water?
questions.ruby_prompt: Before you swim in any water, what should you do?
options: Check it's safe with a grown-up and check the depth
Take a heavy bag with you
questions.expected: Check it's safe with a grown-up and check the depth
questions.memo: Knowing the depth and whether the water is safe (no sharp rocks, no strong currents) protects you before you swim.

questions.question: True or false: Drinking and swimming is safe.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: It is safe for adults to drink alcohol and then swim.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Drinking and swimming is very dangerous — most adult drownings in SA happen after drinking. Tell a parent if you see this happening.

questions.question: Which is a SAFETY ITEM you might find at a public pool?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a safety item you might find at a public pool?
options: A life ring (red and white round float)
questions.expected: A life ring (red and white round float)
questions.memo: Life rings can be thrown to someone in trouble in water. Public pools, dams and beaches often have them.

questions.question: Sipho can't swim. His friends invite him to the dam. What should he do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho can't swim. His friends are going to the dam to play. What should Sipho do?
options: Stay on the bank with a grown-up — and learn to swim with a teacher later
questions.expected: Stay on the bank with a grown-up — and learn to swim with a teacher later
questions.memo: Don't go beyond what you can do. Stay safe, and learn to swim properly with a teacher — most areas have free or cheap lessons.

questions.question: Why are some pools fenced?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why do many home swimming pools have a fence around them?
options: To keep small children and pets from falling in
Because it is the law for no reason
questions.expected: To keep small children and pets from falling in
questions.memo: Pool fences save lives — they stop toddlers and pets from getting to the water unsupervised. Some places make fences a legal requirement.

questions.question: Put these in order if you see someone in trouble in the water.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these steps in order if you see someone in trouble in the water.
options: Shout to a grown-up for help
Throw something they can hold (rope, stick, float)
Keep calling for help until adults come
questions.expected: Shout to a grown-up for help,Throw something they can hold (rope, stick, float),Stay on dry ground yourself,Keep calling for help until adults come
questions.memo: Shout, throw, stay safe yourself, keep calling. Going in yourself often makes you the next casualty.

questions.question: Which is a sign someone is drowning?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a sign that someone is drowning?
options: They are silent and bobbing up and down
They are splashing in a happy way
questions.expected: They are silent and bobbing up and down
questions.memo: Drowning is usually QUIET — people can't shout when they are gasping for air. They bob up and try to climb invisible stairs.

questions.question: After heavy rain, are rivers safer or more dangerous?
questions.ruby_prompt: After heavy rain, are rivers safer or more dangerous to swim in?
