options: More dangerous — water is faster and deeper
questions.expected: More dangerous — water is faster and deeper
questions.memo: Heavy rain makes rivers swell and run faster. Many drownings in SA happen after rain. Stay well back.

questions.question: Tell me one rule to keep yourself safe near water.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one rule you can follow to keep yourself safe near water.
questions.expected: Never swim alone, always with a grown-up watching
questions.memo: Good answers: never swim alone, always swim with a grown-up watching, don't swim after heavy rain, learn to swim, wear a lifejacket when boating.

questions.question: Which of these makes a swimming pool safer for small children?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these makes a swimming pool safer for small children?
options: A grown-up watching and a child-safety fence
Toys floating in the deep end
questions.expected: A grown-up watching and a child-safety fence
questions.memo: An adult always watching, plus a barrier, prevents most accidents involving small children and water.

questions.question: Lerato wants to swim in the sea. What's an extra danger at the sea?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato wants to swim in the sea. What's an extra danger at the sea that's not in a pool?
options: Strong waves and rip currents that pull you out to sea
questions.expected: Strong waves and rip currents that pull you out to sea
questions.memo: The sea has waves and rip currents — narrow streams of water that pull you out fast. Always swim where lifeguards are watching.

questions.question: If a rip current pulls you in the sea, you should:
questions.ruby_prompt: If a rip current pulls you in the sea, you should...
options: Swim across the current (sideways), not against it, until you're out of it
Swim straight back to the shore as hard as you can
questions.expected: Swim across the current (sideways), not against it, until you're out of it
questions.memo: Rip currents are narrow — swimming sideways gets you out. Swimming against a rip just tires you out. Lifeguards teach this everywhere.

questions.question: Why is the buddy system good at a pool?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the 'buddy system' and why is it good at a pool?
options: Two people swim together so one can help or call for help if there is trouble
Only one buddy is allowed to swim
questions.expected: Two people swim together so one can help or call for help if there is trouble
questions.memo: Buddy system = two people, one watches and helps the other. Used by swim teams, scouts and lifeguards around the world.

questions.question: True or false: Floaties (armbands) mean a small child is safe in water and doesn't need watching.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: If a small child has floaties on, they don't need an adult watching.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Floaties can slip off or pop. Even with them, small children must have an adult close enough to touch them in the water.

questions.question: Which is the BEST rule to remember about water?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's the most important rule to remember about water?
options: Water can be dangerous — never swim alone, always tell a grown-up where you are
questions.expected: Water can be dangerous — never swim alone, always tell a grown-up where you are
questions.memo: Respect water. Even shallow water can be dangerous for small children. Adults watching + buddy system + telling someone where you are = safety.

LS.L4.PSW.T11.title: Traffic rules for road users
LS.L4.PSW.T11.description: Pedestrians and cyclists, passenger behaviour, railway safety.
LS.L4.PSW.T11.recovery_strategy: Use scenes from the learner's daily life — walking to school, crossing a road, in a taxi or bakkie. Reinforce: always look, always belt up, never play on tracks.

questions.question: When crossing a road, you should first:
questions.ruby_prompt: When you cross a road, what is the first thing to do?
options: Stop, look both ways and listen
Run as fast as you can
Cross while looking at your phone
questions.expected: Stop, look both ways and listen
questions.memo: Stop, look right, look left, look right again, listen. Then cross when it is clear.

questions.question: Which colour traffic light means STOP?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which colour traffic light means STOP?
questions.expected: Red
questions.memo: Red = stop. Green = go (but still check). Yellow/amber = slow down, the light is about to change.

questions.question: A zebra crossing is:
questions.ruby_prompt: A zebra crossing on the road — what is it for?
options: A safe place for people to cross the road
A place for cars to park
A place for taxis to wait
questions.expected: A safe place for people to cross the road
questions.memo: Black-and-white stripes painted on the road. Cars are supposed to stop for people crossing — but you must still check before stepping in.

questions.question: When you are in a car, you should always wear:
questions.ruby_prompt: When you sit in a car, you should always wear what?
questions.expected: A seatbelt
questions.memo: Seatbelts save lives in a crash. In SA, the law requires everyone to belt up — front and back seats.

questions.question: When riding a bicycle, you should wear:
questions.ruby_prompt: When you ride a bicycle, what should you wear?
questions.expected: A helmet
questions.memo: A helmet protects your head if you fall. Bright clothes help cars see you. Lights at night are also important.

questions.question: Which side of the road do pedestrians walk on if there is no pavement?
questions.ruby_prompt: If there is no pavement, which side of the road do you walk on in South Africa?
options: Facing oncoming traffic (the right-hand side as you walk)
In the middle of the road
questions.expected: Facing oncoming traffic (the right-hand side as you walk)
questions.memo: Facing traffic lets you see cars coming and step aside if needed. SA drives on the LEFT, so walking on the RIGHT means you face them.

questions.question: True or false: It is safe to play on or near railway tracks.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: It is safe to play on or near railway tracks.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Never play on or near railway tracks. Trains can't stop quickly. Many children are killed or seriously injured on tracks every year in SA.

questions.question: What should you do at a railway level crossing?
questions.ruby_prompt: What should you do at a railway level crossing?
options: Stop, look both ways, and only cross when no train is coming
questions.expected: Stop, look both ways, and only cross when no train is coming
questions.memo: Trains move much faster than they look. Stop, look both ways, listen — only cross when you can see clearly that no train is coming.

questions.question: A red triangle road sign usually means:
questions.ruby_prompt: A red triangle on a road sign usually means what?
questions.expected: Warning — be careful
questions.memo: Triangles warn drivers (and pedestrians) about danger ahead — a sharp bend, animals, falling rocks, road works, etc.

questions.question: When walking to school early in the morning or at dusk, you should:
questions.ruby_prompt: When you walk to school early in the morning or in dim light, you should:
options: Wear bright or reflective clothes so drivers can see you
Walk in the middle of the road
questions.expected: Wear bright or reflective clothes so drivers can see you
questions.memo: Drivers can't avoid what they can't see. Bright colours, reflective strips, white items — all help cars see you in low light.

questions.question: Which is good behaviour in a taxi?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is good behaviour as a passenger in a taxi?
options: Sit still, don't distract the driver, wear a seatbelt if there is one
questions.expected: Sit still, don't distract the driver, wear a seatbelt if there is one
questions.memo: A focused driver is a safer driver. Sit, belt up if possible, keep quiet — many taxi crashes happen because drivers were distracted.

questions.question: Cycling on a busy road, you should:
questions.ruby_prompt: When cycling on a busy road, what should you do?
options: Ride in the same direction as traffic and use hand signals
Ride in the middle of the lane
questions.expected: Ride in the same direction as traffic and use hand signals
questions.memo: Cycle the same way as the cars. Stick to the side. Use hand signals when turning so drivers know what you're doing.

questions.question: What is a 'crosswalk' or 'pedestrian crossing' for?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is a pedestrian crossing for?
options: Walking across the road in a safer place
questions.expected: Walking across the road in a safer place
questions.memo: Pedestrian crossings (sometimes zebra-striped) are designed for people to cross more safely. Cars should slow and stop.

questions.question: Put these in the right order for crossing a road safely.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these steps in order for safely crossing a road.
options: Find a safe place to cross
Cross when clear, keep looking and listening
questions.expected: Find a safe place to cross,Stop at the edge,Look both ways and listen,Cross when clear, keep looking and listening
questions.memo: Safe spot, stop, look and listen, cross. The classic 'Green Cross Code' — saves lives everywhere.

questions.question: If you are too small to be seen behind a parked car, what should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: If you are too small to be seen behind a parked car, what should you do?
options: Cross away from parked cars, where drivers can see you
questions.expected: Cross away from parked cars, where drivers can see you
questions.memo: Parked cars hide you from drivers. Find an open spot to cross — somewhere drivers can actually see you coming.

questions.question: Mpho is walking on a busy road. A friend phones her. What should she do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho is walking on a busy road and her friend phones her. What should she do?
options: Step off the road into a safe spot before answering
Answer while walking with no looking
questions.expected: Step off the road into a safe spot before answering
questions.memo: Phones distract you. Step off the road first, talk in a safe place, then walk on. Most pedestrian accidents involve distraction.

questions.question: True or false: You should always sit in a vehicle with a seatbelt on.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: You should always sit with a seatbelt on in a vehicle.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Seatbelts halve your chance of being seriously injured in a crash. SA law requires belts when fitted.

questions.question: Tell me one road safety rule for pedestrians.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one road safety rule for pedestrians (people walking).
questions.expected: Stop, look both ways and listen before crossing
questions.memo: Good answers: stop and look both ways, use a crossing, wear bright colours at dusk, walk facing traffic if no pavement, don't use a phone while crossing.

questions.question: Which is SAFER to do on a bakkie (pickup truck)?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is safer when you travel in a bakkie (pickup truck)?
options: Sit inside the cab with a seatbelt on
questions.expected: Sit inside the cab with a seatbelt on
questions.memo: Riding on the open back of a bakkie is dangerous — a sudden brake or turn can throw people out. Inside with a seatbelt is far safer.

questions.question: Why are railway tracks especially dangerous?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why are railway tracks especially dangerous places?
options: Trains are heavy and fast and can't stop quickly
questions.expected: Trains are heavy and fast and can't stop quickly
questions.memo: A train takes hundreds of metres to stop. By the time the driver sees you, it's too late. Stay well clear of tracks — always.

LS.L4.PSW.T12.title: Personal and household hygiene
LS.L4.PSW.T12.description: Personal hygiene items that cannot be shared, germ breeding areas in the house.
LS.L4.PSW.T12.recovery_strategy: Keep tone matter-of-fact. Hygiene is a daily habit, not a punishment. Help the learner identify which items stay personal and which germs hide in.

questions.question: Which of these is a personal hygiene item that should NOT be shared?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a personal hygiene item that should NOT be shared?
questions.expected: A toothbrush
questions.memo: Toothbrushes touch your mouth and carry germs. Each person needs their own.

questions.question: Why shouldn't you share a face towel?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why shouldn't you share a face towel?
options: It can spread skin infections and germs
questions.expected: It can spread skin infections and germs
questions.memo: Face towels carry skin germs. Sharing them can spread infections like pink-eye (conjunctivitis) or skin rashes.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a personal item — it IS okay to share?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is okay to share?
questions.expected: A book
questions.memo: Books, sports equipment, toys are fine to share. Items that touch your skin, mouth, eyes or private parts should stay personal.

questions.question: Where do germs LOVE to grow in a house?
questions.ruby_prompt: Where do germs love to grow in a house?
options: In warm, damp places like dirty kitchens and bathrooms
questions.expected: In warm, damp places like dirty kitchens and bathrooms
questions.memo: Germs need warmth, food and moisture to grow. Dirty dishes, food crumbs, damp bathrooms — all favourites.

questions.question: Put these steps in order for washing your hands well.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these steps in the right order for washing your hands.
options: Rub for 20 seconds, including thumbs and nails
Rinse and dry on a clean towel
questions.expected: Wet your hands,Use soap,Rub for 20 seconds, including thumbs and nails,Rinse and dry on a clean towel
questions.memo: Wet, soap, scrub all over for 20 seconds, rinse, dry. Hand-washing prevents many illnesses.

questions.question: When should you wash your hands?
questions.ruby_prompt: When are important times to wash your hands?
options: Before eating, after the toilet, and after coughing or sneezing
questions.expected: Before eating, after the toilet, and after coughing or sneezing
questions.memo: These three times stop most germs from getting into your body or onto others'.

questions.question: True or false: Brushing teeth twice a day keeps mouths healthy.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Brushing teeth twice a day helps keep your mouth healthy.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Twice a day — morning and night — is the standard. Don't forget the back teeth and along the gumline.

questions.question: Which is a 'germ-breeding area' in a kitchen?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a germ-breeding area in a kitchen?
questions.expected: A dirty dishcloth or sponge
questions.memo: Dishcloths and sponges hold food bits, water and germs. They should be rinsed, dried in the sun, and replaced often.

questions.question: Which bathroom item is a germ-breeding area if not cleaned?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which bathroom item becomes a germ-breeding area if it isn't cleaned?
questions.expected: The toilet seat and bowl
questions.memo: Toilets have lots of germs. Cleaning them with a brush and disinfectant regularly keeps the whole bathroom safer.

questions.question: Sipho coughs into his hand and then shakes a friend's hand. What's wrong?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho coughs into his hand and then shakes a friend's hand. What's wrong with that?
options: He's passed germs straight to his friend
questions.expected: He's passed germs straight to his friend
questions.memo: Cough/sneeze into your elbow or a tissue, not your hand. Then wash. That cuts the chain of germs.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep your nails short and clean?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why are short clean nails important for hygiene?
options: Germs and dirt collect under long nails
Long nails make you sick by themselves
questions.expected: Germs and dirt collect under long nails
questions.memo: Under-nail dirt is a real germ hideout. Trim, wash and dry under the nails — especially before eating.

questions.question: Which of these is a good daily hygiene habit?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a good daily hygiene habit?
options: Bathe or wash daily and wear clean clothes
questions.expected: Bathe or wash daily and wear clean clothes
questions.memo: A daily wash and clean clothes keep skin healthy and prevent body odour and infections.

questions.question: Sharing a toothbrush spreads:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sharing a toothbrush mostly spreads what?
options: Mouth germs and possible diseases like colds and gum infections
questions.expected: Mouth germs and possible diseases like colds and gum infections
questions.memo: Toothbrushes hold mouth germs — including those that cause colds, flu and even some serious infections. Always your own.

questions.question: Sun-drying laundry helps because:
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is sun-drying laundry good?
questions.expected: Sunlight kills many germs
questions.memo: UV rays from the sun kill many germs. Sun-drying — especially towels and bedding — adds free disinfecting.

questions.question: True or false: It is okay to put your finger in your eye after touching dirty things.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: It is okay to touch your eye with a finger that has touched dirty things.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Eyes are an easy way for germs to enter the body. Wash hands before touching your face or eyes.

questions.question: Karabo finds an old toothbrush on the floor. What should she do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Karabo finds an old toothbrush lying on the floor. What should she do?
options: Throw it away — used toothbrushes are personal and used ones aren't safe
Put it in her own cup
questions.expected: Throw it away — used toothbrushes are personal and used ones aren't safe
questions.memo: Old toothbrushes carry germs and aren't yours. Bin them. Always start with a new clean brush of your own.

questions.question: Why is it important to flush the toilet and close the lid before flushing?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it important to flush the toilet AND close the lid before flushing?
options: Flushing without a lid can spray germs into the air
questions.expected: Flushing without a lid can spray germs into the air
questions.memo: When a toilet flushes, tiny droplets fly out. Closing the lid keeps those droplets from landing on your toothbrush etc.

questions.question: Which is a good rule for keeping food safe in the house?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a good rule for keeping food safe in the house?
options: Cover food and keep raw meat away from cooked food
Put raw chicken on top of fruit
questions.expected: Cover food and keep raw meat away from cooked food
questions.memo: Covering food keeps flies and germs out. Raw meat juices carry germs — keep them away from food that won't be cooked again.

questions.question: Tell me one personal item you should NOT share.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one personal item you should never share with someone else.
questions.expected: A toothbrush
questions.memo: Good answers: toothbrush, comb/brush, face towel, underwear, socks, drinking cup, ear-cleaning items. Anything that touches your private skin, mouth or eyes.

questions.question: Which sequence shows how germs spread from a dirty hand to make you sick?
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in the right order to show how germs from a dirty hand can make you sick.
questions.expected: Hand touches a dirty thing,Hand touches food or face,Germs enter the body,Person gets sick
questions.memo: Dirty thing → hand → food/face → inside body → sickness. Washing breaks the chain at the hand stage.

LS.L4.PSW.T13.title: Dietary habits of children
LS.L4.PSW.T13.description: Impact of dietary habits on dental and oral hygiene.
LS.L4.PSW.T13.recovery_strategy: Focus on the link between everyday food choices and how teeth feel. Avoid shaming favourite foods — frame as 'how often' and 'what to do after'.

questions.question: Which of these is bad for your teeth if eaten very often?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is bad for your teeth if eaten very often?
questions.expected: Sweets and sugary fizzy drinks
questions.memo: Sugar feeds the germs in your mouth that cause tooth decay. Sweets and fizzy drinks are the biggest culprits.

questions.question: How many times a day should you brush your teeth?
questions.ruby_prompt: How many times a day should you brush your teeth?
questions.expected: Twice a day
questions.memo: Morning and night. Brushing twice a day with fluoride toothpaste protects your teeth.

questions.question: Which is BEST for your teeth to drink?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is best for your teeth to drink?
questions.expected: Water
questions.memo: Water has no sugar and helps wash food bits away. The best drink for your teeth and the rest of your body.

questions.question: What causes a 'cavity' (a hole in a tooth)?
questions.ruby_prompt: What causes a cavity — a hole in a tooth?
options: Germs that eat sugar on the teeth and produce acid
questions.expected: Germs that eat sugar on the teeth and produce acid
questions.memo: Mouth germs use leftover sugar to make acid. The acid eats away at the tooth, causing a cavity. Brushing removes both.

questions.question: True or false: Eating fruit between meals is better for teeth than eating sweets.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Eating fruit between meals is better for your teeth than eating sweets.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. Fruit has natural sugar but also fibre and water. Sweets are concentrated sugar that sticks to teeth.

questions.question: Which is a HEALTHY snack for between meals?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is a healthy snack to have between meals?
questions.expected: An apple or a carrot
questions.memo: Fruit and crunchy vegetables clean teeth a little while you chew, and give your body real nutrition.

questions.question: Which food contains LOTS of hidden sugar?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these has lots of hidden sugar?
questions.expected: Sweetened cold drink (cola, fanta)
questions.memo: One can of fizzy drink can have 8–10 teaspoons of sugar. That's why dentists worry about them most.

questions.question: What does FLUORIDE in toothpaste do?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does fluoride — the medicine in toothpaste — do?
options: Makes the outer layer of teeth stronger
questions.expected: Makes the outer layer of teeth stronger
questions.memo: Fluoride strengthens tooth enamel — the hard outer layer. Look for it on toothpaste labels.

questions.question: Lerato eats sweets all day at school. Her teeth start to hurt. What does she need to do?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato eats sweets all day at school. Her teeth start to hurt. What does she need to do?
options: See a dentist and cut down on sweets, brush twice a day
questions.expected: See a dentist and cut down on sweets, brush twice a day
questions.memo: Pain often means decay. Visit the dentist; in the meantime cut sweets, brush properly, and drink water.

questions.question: Which is true about milk for teeth?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is true about milk and teeth?
options: Milk has calcium which helps teeth and bones grow strong
Milk has lots of bad sugar
questions.expected: Milk has calcium which helps teeth and bones grow strong
questions.memo: Calcium is the mineral your teeth and bones are made of. Milk and yoghurt are good sources.

questions.question: Put these in order for brushing your teeth properly.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these steps in order for brushing your teeth properly.
options: Put a pea-size of toothpaste on the brush
Brush all sides of every tooth for 2 minutes
Rinse the brush and put it away to dry
questions.expected: Put a pea-size of toothpaste on the brush,Brush all sides of every tooth for 2 minutes,Spit out the toothpaste,Rinse the brush and put it away to dry
questions.memo: Pea-sized blob, two minutes covering ALL sides, spit don't rinse the mouth (so fluoride stays), clean brush.

questions.question: True or false: If you eat well, you never need to see a dentist.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: If you eat healthy food, you never need to see a dentist.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Even healthy eaters need check-ups — once or twice a year. A dentist spots small problems before they become big ones.

questions.question: Sipho's mouth feels sticky after sweets. Why?
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho's mouth feels sticky after sweets. Why?
options: Sugar coats his teeth and feeds the germs
questions.expected: Sugar coats his teeth and feeds the germs
questions.memo: Stickiness = sugar coating teeth. Rinsing with water or brushing soon after helps cut the damage.

questions.question: After eating, what's a quick thing you can do for your teeth if you can't brush?
questions.ruby_prompt: After eating, what's a quick thing you can do for your teeth if you can't brush right away?
questions.expected: Rinse your mouth with water
questions.memo: Water rinses sugar and food bits off your teeth. Best second-best when a brush isn't there.

questions.question: Which is BEST as a lunch-pack drink for school?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is the best drink to pack for school?
questions.expected: Water
questions.memo: Water for thirst, every day. Save sweet drinks for special occasions, not for school lunches.

questions.question: Sticky sweets are worse than chocolate that melts away because:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sticky sweets are worse for teeth than chocolate that melts away. Why?
options: Sticky sweets cling to teeth for longer, giving germs more time to make acid
questions.expected: Sticky sweets cling to teeth for longer, giving germs more time to make acid
questions.memo: Stickiness extends the damage time. Caramel, toffee and gummies stay on teeth for ages — that's a long acid attack.

questions.question: Tell me one healthy snack you like.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one healthy snack that you like.
questions.expected: An apple
questions.memo: Good answers: fresh fruit (apple, banana, orange, pear), raw veg (carrot, cucumber), nuts (if no allergy), plain yoghurt, biltong (in moderation).

questions.question: Which group of food helps keep your gums healthy?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which food group helps keep your gums healthy?
questions.expected: Fruits and vegetables (vitamin C)
questions.memo: Vitamin C in fruit and veg keeps gums strong. Without it, gums can bleed and teeth can loosen.

questions.question: Why is going to bed without brushing especially bad?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is going to sleep without brushing your teeth especially bad?
options: Germs work on sugar all night while you sleep
questions.expected: Germs work on sugar all night while you sleep
questions.memo: While you sleep, less saliva flows. Germs have a long quiet party with any sugar left on your teeth. Always brush before bed.

questions.question: Mpho eats sweets daily AND never brushes. What is most likely to happen?
questions.ruby_prompt: Mpho eats sweets every day AND never brushes her teeth. What is most likely to happen?
options: Cavities, tooth pain and possibly losing teeth
questions.expected: Cavities, tooth pain and possibly losing teeth
questions.memo: The combination of constant sugar plus no brushing is the recipe for tooth decay. Even children can lose adult teeth this way.

LS.L4.PSW.T14.title: Healthy environment and personal health
LS.L4.PSW.T14.description: Home, school and community. Unhealthy environments (air, water, land pollution, illegal dumping), dangers to personal health, conservation strategies, Arbor Day.
LS.L4.PSW.T14.recovery_strategy: Connect the environment to the learner's daily life and health — air at home, water from the tap, litter outside the gate. Small actions matter.

questions.question: What is 'pollution'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does the word 'pollution' mean?
options: Dirt or harmful things in the air, water or land
questions.expected: Dirt or harmful things in the air, water or land
questions.memo: Pollution is anything harmful in our environment — smoke, plastic, dirty water, chemicals.

questions.question: Which is an example of LAND pollution?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is an example of land pollution?
options: Plastic bottles and rubbish thrown on the ground
questions.expected: Plastic bottles and rubbish thrown on the ground
questions.memo: Land pollution = rubbish on the ground. Plastics last hundreds of years and harm animals that eat or get tangled in them.

questions.question: Which is an example of WATER pollution?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is an example of water pollution?
options: Factory chemicals or sewage in a river
Children playing in a clean pool
questions.expected: Factory chemicals or sewage in a river
questions.memo: Water pollution = harmful things in our water — factory waste, sewage, oil. It kills fish and can make people very sick.

questions.question: Which is an example of AIR pollution?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is an example of air pollution?
options: Smoke from factories, fires and many cars
questions.expected: Smoke from factories, fires and many cars
questions.memo: Smoke and exhaust fumes pollute air. Long-term, polluted air causes lung diseases and worsens asthma.

questions.question: What is an 'illegal dumping site'?
questions.ruby_prompt: What is an illegal dumping site?
options: A place where people dump rubbish where they shouldn't
questions.expected: A place where people dump rubbish where they shouldn't
questions.memo: When people dump waste somewhere that isn't a proper rubbish site — empty land, riverbanks, vacant plots — it harms the area and is against the law.

questions.question: Why is illegal dumping bad for health?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is illegal dumping bad for our health?
options: Rotting rubbish attracts rats, flies and disease
It makes the area look nicer
questions.expected: Rotting rubbish attracts rats, flies and disease
questions.memo: Dumped rubbish breeds rats, flies and mosquitoes, which spread disease. It also pollutes water and soil.

questions.question: True or false: One person picking up litter doesn't matter.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: One person picking up litter doesn't really matter.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Every piece of litter picked up is one piece less harming the environment. And one person often inspires others.

questions.question: Which is a way to keep your home environment HEALTHY?
questions.ruby_prompt: What's a way to keep your home environment healthy?
options: Empty bins, sweep, and let fresh air in
questions.expected: Empty bins, sweep, and let fresh air in
questions.memo: Clean surfaces, regular bin emptying, and ventilation keep a home healthy. Trapped damp and dust cause illness.

questions.question: What does 'conservation' mean?
questions.ruby_prompt: What does 'conservation' mean?
options: Looking after and protecting nature for the future
questions.expected: Looking after and protecting nature for the future
questions.memo: Conservation = caring for water, trees, soil and wildlife so they last. It's how the planet stays able to look after us.

questions.question: Arbor Day is a day for:
questions.ruby_prompt: Arbor Day is a day for what?
questions.expected: Planting and caring for trees
questions.memo: Arbor Day (in early September in SA) is when schools and communities plant trees. Trees clean air and give shade.

questions.question: Which is a way to use LESS water at home?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is a way to use less water at home?
options: Take shorter showers and fix leaks
Wash one dish in lots of water
questions.expected: Take shorter showers and fix leaks
questions.memo: Short showers, fixed leaks, full loads in the washing machine — small habits that save big amounts of water.

questions.question: Why are trees important for our environment?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why are trees so important for our environment?
options: They clean the air, give shade, and prevent soil from washing away
questions.expected: They clean the air, give shade, and prevent soil from washing away
questions.memo: Trees clean air, hold soil, give shade, cool cities, and make oxygen. One mature tree does a lot of work.

questions.question: Which is a kind of recycling?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is recycling?
options: Putting plastic bottles and paper in special bins to be reused
questions.expected: Putting plastic bottles and paper in special bins to be reused
questions.memo: Recycling = turning used things into new things. Many SA towns have recycling pickers — sorting helps them.

questions.question: Put these in order for what to do with an empty plastic bottle.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for what you should do with an empty plastic bottle.
options: Crush it to take less space
Put it in a recycling bin or hand it to a recycler
questions.expected: Empty out any liquid,Crush it to take less space,Put it in a recycling bin or hand it to a recycler,Don't litter or burn it
questions.memo: Empty, crush, recycle — and never burn (smoke from plastic is poisonous).

questions.question: True or false: Burning plastic at home is a good way to get rid of it.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Burning plastic at home is a good way to get rid of it.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Burning plastic releases poisonous smoke that harms your lungs. Recycle or take to a proper waste site.

questions.question: Sipho lives near an illegal dumping site. His chest is often sore. The link is:
questions.ruby_prompt: Sipho lives near an illegal dumping site. His chest is often sore. What's the link?
options: Burning rubbish and dust can hurt his lungs
questions.expected: Burning rubbish and dust can hurt his lungs
questions.memo: Dust and smoke from dumps trigger coughs, asthma and chest problems. Cleaning up dumps is a health issue, not just looks.

questions.question: Tell me one thing you can do to look after the environment.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one thing you can do to look after the environment.
questions.expected: Pick up litter when I see it
questions.memo: Good answers: pick up litter, use bins, plant a tree, save water, recycle, walk or cycle short distances, don't litter.

questions.question: When is South African Arbor Day usually celebrated?
questions.ruby_prompt: When is South African Arbor Day (or Arbor Week) usually celebrated?
questions.expected: Early September each year
questions.memo: Arbor Week is in early September in SA — the start of spring, the right time to plant.

questions.question: A community clean-up day helps because:
questions.ruby_prompt: Why does a community clean-up day help?
options: Many hands remove a lot of litter and people care more afterwards
questions.expected: Many hands remove a lot of litter and people care more afterwards
questions.memo: Group clean-ups remove lots of waste fast AND change the community's attitude — people are less likely to litter a place they've cleaned.

questions.question: Which is the BEST description of a healthy environment?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which is the best description of a healthy environment?
options: Clean air, clean water, trees and green spaces, no rubbish
questions.expected: Clean air, clean water, trees and green spaces, no rubbish
questions.memo: Healthy = clean air, clean water, places for plants and wildlife, and waste handled properly. It supports our health too.

LS.L4.PSW.T15.title: HIV and AIDS: basic facts
LS.L4.PSW.T15.description: Basic explanation of HIV and AIDS, transmission through blood, how HIV is not transmitted, protecting oneself against infection through blood.
LS.L4.PSW.T15.recovery_strategy: Be factual and calm. HIV is treatable. Reinforce: people with HIV are not 'bad' or 'dangerous'; you cannot catch HIV from everyday contact like hugging, sharing food or sitting next to someone.

questions.question: What does HIV stand for in short?
questions.ruby_prompt: HIV is a name for a virus. What does HIV stand for, very simply?
options: Human Immunodeficiency Virus — it weakens the body's protection
questions.expected: Human Immunodeficiency Virus — it weakens the body's protection
questions.memo: HIV is a virus. It attacks the body's immune system — the part that fights off germs. People can live with HIV with proper medicine.

questions.question: What does AIDS stand for in short?
questions.ruby_prompt: AIDS is a condition that can happen if HIV is not treated. What does AIDS mean simply?
options: Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome — when the body can no longer fight off many illnesses
questions.expected: Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome — when the body can no longer fight off many illnesses
questions.memo: AIDS happens later, only if HIV is not treated. With good medicine, people with HIV may never get AIDS.

questions.question: Can you catch HIV from hugging someone with HIV?
questions.ruby_prompt: Can you catch HIV from hugging someone who has HIV?
options: No — HIV is not spread by everyday contact like hugging
questions.expected: No — HIV is not spread by everyday contact like hugging
questions.memo: HIV is NOT in sweat, saliva, tears or air. Hugs, handshakes, sharing meals, sitting together, swimming pools — all completely safe.

questions.question: Can you catch HIV from sharing food or a cup with someone who has HIV?
questions.ruby_prompt: Can you catch HIV from sharing food or a cup with someone who has HIV?
options: Only if you eat all the food
questions.expected: No
questions.memo: Sharing food, drinks, plates, cups — none of these spread HIV. Children with HIV are safe to be with at school.

questions.question: True or false: A person with HIV can take medicine and live a long healthy life.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: A person with HIV can take medicine and live a long healthy life.
questions.expected: true
questions.memo: Yes. HIV medicine (called ARVs) is free in SA. People who take it daily can live full long lives.

questions.question: One way HIV CAN spread through blood is:
questions.ruby_prompt: One way HIV can spread between people is through blood. Which is an example?
options: Using a needle that already had someone else's blood on it
questions.expected: Using a needle that already had someone else's blood on it
questions.memo: HIV spreads through certain body fluids, especially blood. Used needles are one way — never touch a needle you find.

questions.question: If you see a used needle on the ground, what should you do?
questions.ruby_prompt: If you see a used needle lying on the ground, what should you do?
options: Tell a grown-up — never pick it up yourself
Pick it up to look at it
questions.expected: Tell a grown-up — never pick it up yourself
questions.memo: Needles can have blood on them and carry HIV or other diseases. Tell an adult — they will dispose of it safely.

questions.question: If a friend is bleeding and needs help, what should you do safely?
questions.ruby_prompt: Your friend is bleeding. They need help. How can you help safely?
options: Tell a grown-up and use a clean cloth, gloves if you have them
Touch the blood with your bare hands
questions.expected: Tell a grown-up and use a clean cloth, gloves if you have them
questions.memo: Get an adult. If you must help quickly, use a cloth between your hand and the wound — gloves are even better. Always wash your hands afterwards.

questions.question: True or false: You can tell if someone has HIV by looking at them.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: You can tell if someone has HIV just by looking at them.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: You cannot tell. People with HIV look like everyone else. The only way to know is a blood test.

questions.question: Where can a person be tested for HIV in South Africa?
questions.ruby_prompt: Where in South Africa can a person be tested for HIV?
options: At any government clinic — testing is free and private
Only at one hospital in the whole country
Only by paying lots of money
questions.expected: At any government clinic — testing is free and private
questions.memo: Free, private HIV tests are at all government clinics. Many also offer ARVs free if needed.

questions.question: A child at school has HIV. The right thing for classmates to do is:
questions.ruby_prompt: A child at school has HIV. What's the right thing for classmates to do?
options: Treat them like any other friend — they cannot infect you in normal play
questions.expected: Treat them like any other friend — they cannot infect you in normal play
questions.memo: Children with HIV go to school like everyone else. HIV doesn't spread through everyday play. Kindness matters most.

questions.question: Why is it important NOT to make fun of people with HIV?
questions.ruby_prompt: Why is it important not to make fun of someone with HIV?
options: People with HIV are sick because of a virus, not because they did anything wrong — they need our care
Because it's illegal to be kind
questions.expected: People with HIV are sick because of a virus, not because they did anything wrong — they need our care
questions.memo: HIV is a virus, not a punishment. Making fun adds pain and stops people from getting tested and treated. Stigma kills.

questions.question: Which is NOT a way HIV spreads?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these is NOT a way that HIV spreads?
options: Used needles with blood on them
Mother to baby during birth without medicine
questions.expected: Mosquito bites
questions.memo: Mosquitoes can spread malaria but not HIV. HIV spreads through specific body fluids — blood, mother-to-baby fluids, and sexual fluids.

questions.question: What are 'ARVs' (the medicine for HIV)?
questions.ruby_prompt: What are ARVs — the medicine for HIV?
options: Pills that stop HIV from making people sick
questions.expected: Pills that stop HIV from making people sick
questions.memo: Antiretrovirals (ARVs) are taken daily to keep HIV under control. South Africa has the largest ARV programme in the world — it's free.

questions.question: Put these in order for what to do if you see blood on a cut or grazes.
questions.ruby_prompt: Put these in order for what to do if you see blood from a cut.
options: Use a cloth or gloves to press on the cut
questions.expected: Don't touch the blood directly,Call or fetch a grown-up,Use a cloth or gloves to press on the cut,Wash your hands well afterwards
questions.memo: Don't touch, get an adult, protect your hands while helping, wash. This is good hygiene AND prevents HIV through blood.

questions.question: True or false: Sharing a toothbrush with someone with HIV is safe.
questions.ruby_prompt: True or false: Sharing a toothbrush with someone with HIV is safe.
questions.expected: false
questions.memo: Toothbrushes can have tiny amounts of blood from gums on them. Sharing them is one of the few in-the-home risks. Each person their own — always.

questions.question: Lerato hears a rumour that you can get HIV from a swimming pool. What's true?
questions.ruby_prompt: Lerato hears a rumour that you can get HIV from a swimming pool. What's the truth?
options: You cannot — HIV does not spread through water, pools, taps or showers
questions.expected: You cannot — HIV does not spread through water, pools, taps or showers
questions.memo: HIV doesn't survive in water. Pools, taps, baths — all safe. Many myths about HIV exist; the clinic and your teacher have the facts.

questions.question: Tell me one way HIV does NOT spread.
questions.ruby_prompt: Tell me one way that HIV does NOT spread.
questions.expected: Hugging or shaking hands
questions.memo: Good answers: hugging, handshakes, sharing food/cups, mosquito bites, sitting in class together, swimming pools, sneezing, sweat, tears.

questions.question: If a classmate has HIV and a learner says something unkind, the right thing to do is:
questions.ruby_prompt: If a classmate has HIV and someone says something unkind about them, what's the right thing to do?
options: Tell them HIV doesn't spread by everyday contact and report it to a teacher
questions.expected: Tell them HIV doesn't spread by everyday contact and report it to a teacher
questions.memo: Speaking up against stigma protects everyone. Teachers and counsellors help — and people with HIV are people who need friends.

questions.question: Which sentence is TRUE about HIV today?
questions.ruby_prompt: Which of these statements is true about HIV today?
options: HIV can be treated. People with HIV who take ARVs daily can live full long lives.
HIV is always fatal in a year.
HIV is contagious in the air.
questions.expected: HIV can be treated. People with HIV who take ARVs daily can live full long lives.
questions.memo: ARVs changed everything. With daily medicine, HIV is now a long-term condition like diabetes — manageable, not a death sentence.
